Isoprenoids are essential in all organisms, and can also be synthesized through the mevalonate pathway. The non-mevolante route is used by many bacteria and human pathogens, including Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Plasmodium falcipar
IPR036571.name: 2-C-methyl-D-erythritol 2,4-cyclodiphosphate synthase superfamily

IPR036573.description: A carbohydrate-binding module (CBM) is defined as a contiguous amino acid sequence within a carbohydrate-active enzyme with a discreet fold having carbohydrate-binding activity. A few exceptions are CBMs in cellulosomal scaffolding proteins and rare instances of independent putative CBMs. The requirement of CBMs existing as modules within larger enzymes sets this class of carbohydrate-binding prot
IPR036573.name: Carbohydrate-binding module superfamily 5/12

IPR036575.name: Transcription elongation factor S-II, central domain superfamily

IPR036577.description: Photosystem I (PSI) is an integral membrane protein complex that uses light energy to mediate electron transfer from plastocyanin to ferredoxin. Subunit III (or PsaF) is one of at least 14 different subunits that compose the photosystem I reaction centre (PSI-RC).
IPR036577.name: Photosystem I PsaF, reaction centre subunit III superfamily

IPR036579.description: PsaD is a small, extrinsic polypeptide located on the stromal side (cytoplasmic side in cyanobacteria) of the photosystem I reaction centre complex. It is required for native assembly of PSI reaction clusters and is implicated in the electrostatic binding of ferredoxin within the reaction centre. PsaD forms a dimer in solution which is bound by PsaE however PsaD is monomeric in its native complexe
IPR036579.name: Photosystem I, reaction centre subunit PsaD superfamily

IPR036581.description: Some bacteria can overcome the toxicity of environmental cyanate by hydrolysis of cyanate. This reaction is catalyzed by cyanate lyase (also known as cyanase). Cyanate lyase is found in bacteria and plants and catalyzes the reaction of cyanate with bicarbonate to produce ammonia and carbon dioxide.
IPR036581.name: Cyanate lyase, C-terminal domain superfamily

IPR036582.name: Copper amine oxidase-like, N-terminal domain superfamily

IPR036583.description: This superfamily consists of bacterial proteins encoded within an intervening sequence present within some 23S rRNA genes. It folds into an anti-parallel four-helix bundle and forms homopentamers.
IPR036583.name: 23S rRNA-intervening sequence superfamily

IPR036584.description: The fliD operon of several bacteria consists of three flagellar genes, fliD, fliS, and fliT, and is transcribed in this order. In Bacillus subtilis the operon encoding the flagellar proteins FliD, FliS, and FliT is sigma D-dependent.
IPR036584.name: Flagellar protein FliS superfamily

IPR036588.description: This entry represents CbiC and CobH precorrin-8X methylmutase (), both as stand-alone enzymes and when CobJ forms part of a bifunctional enzyme. CobH and CbiC from the aerobic and anaerobic pathways, respectively, catalyse a methyl rearrangement in precorrin-8 that moves the methyl group from C-11 to C-12 to produce hydrogenobyrinic acid. Hydrogenobyrinic acid now contains all the major framework
IPR036588.name: Precorrin-8X methylmutase CobH/CbiC superfamily

IPR036589.description: The homocysteine (Hcy) binding domain is an ~300-residue module which is found in a set of enzymes involved in alkyl transfer to thiols:
IPR036589.name: Homocysteine-binding domain superfamily

IPR036590.description: This entry represents the SOS response associated peptidase (SRAP) superfamily.
IPR036590.name: SOS response associated peptidase-like

IPR036591.description: This entry, previously known as DUF167, describes a group of proteins found in all cellular organisms. A member of this family, PF1765 protein from Pyrococcus furiosus was structurally and functionally characterised. PF1765 binds variably to dsDNA, ssDNA, and RNA, with a modest preference for single-stranded substrates. Structures for two of other proteins, YggU from Escherichia coli and MTH637 fr
IPR036591.name: YggU-like superfamily

IPR036592.description: The trimeric photosystem I of the cyanobacterium Synechococcus elongatus recomprises 11 protein subunits. Subunit XI, PsaL, from plants and bacteria is one of the smaller subunits with only two transmembrane α helices. PsaL interacts closely with PsaI.
IPR036592.name: Photosystem I PsaL, reaction centre subunit XI superfamily

IPR036594.description: Cobalamin-dependent methionine synthase () is a large modular protein that catalyses methyl transfer from methyltetrahydrofolate (CH3-H4folate) to homocysteine. During the catalytic cycle, it supports three distinct methyl transfer reactions, each involving the cobalamin (vitamin B12) cofactor and a substrate bound to its own functional unit. The cobalamin cofactor plays an essential role in this
IPR036594.name: Methionine synthase domain

IPR036596.description: Bacterial cytochrome c oxidase is found bound to the to the cell membrane, where it is involved in the generation of the transmembrane proton electrochemical gradient. It is composed of four subunits. Subunit IV consists of one transmembrane helix that does not interact directly with the other subunits, but maintains its position by indirect contacts via phospholipid molecules found in the structu
IPR036596.name: Bacterial aa3 type cytochrome c oxidase subunit IV superfamily

IPR036597.description: This globular domain is named fido after the Fic and Doc proteins where it is found. It is approximately 125 to 150 residues long, and is present in proteins from all kingdoms of life, including:
IPR036597.name: Fido-like domain superfamily

IPR036599.description: DNA ligase (polydeoxyribonucleotide synthase) is the enzyme that joins two DNA fragments by catalysing the formation of an internucleotide ester bond between phosphate and deoxyribose. It is active during DNA replication, DNA repair and DNA recombination. There are two forms of DNA ligase, one requires ATP (), the other NAD (), the latter being restricted to eubacteria. Eukaryotic, archaebacterial
IPR036599.name: DNA ligase, ATP-dependent, N-terminal domain superfamily

IPR036603.description: RNA polymerase (RNAP) II, which is responsible for all mRNA synthesis in eukaryotes, consists of 12 subunits. Subunits Rpb3 and Rpb11 form a heterodimer that is functionally analogous to the archaeal RNAP D/L heterodimer, and the prokaryotic RNAP alpha subunit homodimer. In each case, they play a key role in RNAP assembly by forming a platform on which the catalytic subunits (eukaryotic Rpb1/Rpb2,
IPR036603.name: RNA polymerase, RBP11-like subunit

IPR036604.description: Phosphoribosylformylglycinamidine(FGAM) synthetase,, catalyses the fourth step in the de novo purine biosynthetic pathway.
IPR036604.name: Phosphoribosylformylglycinamidine synthase subunit PurS-like superfamily

IPR036609.description: The LCCL domain has been named after the best characterised proteins that were found to contain it, namely Limulus factor C, Coch-5b2 and Lgl1. It is an about 100 amino acids domain whose C-terminal part contains a highly conserved histidine in a conserved motif YxxxSxxCxAAVHxGVI. The LCCL module is thought to be an autonomously folding domain that has been used for the construction of various mod
IPR036609.name: LCCL domain superfamily

IPR036610.description: The PEBP (PhosphatidylEthanolamine-Binding Protein) superfamily is a highly conserved group of proteins that have been identified in numerous tissues in a wide variety of organisms, including bacteria, yeast, nematodes, plants, drosophila and mammals. The various functions described for members of this family include lipid binding, neuronal development, serine protease inhibition, the control of t
IPR036610.name: PEBP-like superfamily

IPR036611.description: In the Escherichia coli cytosol, a fraction of the newly synthesised proteins requires the activity of molecular chaperones for folding to the native state. The major chaperones implicated in this folding process are the ribosome-associated Trigger Factor (TF), and the DnaK and GroEL chaperones with their respective co-chaperones. Trigger Factor is an ATP-independent chaperone and displays chapero
IPR036611.name: Trigger factor ribosome-binding domain superfamily

IPR036612.description: The K homology (KH) domain was first identified in the human heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein (hnRNP) K. It is a domain of around 70 amino acids that is present in a wide variety of quite diverse nucleic acid-binding proteins. It has been shown to bind RNA. Like many other RNA-binding motifs, KH motifs are found in one or multiple copies (14 copies in chicken vigilin) and, at least for hnRN
IPR036612.name: K Homology domain, type 1 superfamily

IPR036613.name: MHC class II-associated invariant chain, trimerisation domain superfamily

IPR036614.description: This superfamily consists of several bacterial and phage Holliday junction resolvase (RusA) like proteins. The RusA protein of Escherichia coli is an endonuclease that can resolve Holliday intermediates and correct the defects in genetic recombination and DNA repair associated with inactivation of RuvAB or RuvC.
IPR036614.name: Holliday junction resolvase RusA-like superfamily

IPR036615.description: This entry represents the C-terminal domain superfamily from all four stage 2 Mur enzymes: UDP-N-acetylmuramate-L-alanine ligase (MurC), UDP-N-acetylmuramoylalanine-D-glutamate ligase (MurD), UDP-N-acetylmuramoylalanyl-D-glutamate-2,6-diaminopimelate ligase (MurE), and UDP-N-acetylmuramoyl-tripeptide-D-alanyl-D-alanine ligase (MurF). This entry also includes the C-terminal domain of folylpolygluta
IPR036615.name: Mur ligase, C-terminal domain superfamily

IPR036618.description: This superfamily describes a domain that can be found in the N terminus of PtsI, a component of the phosphoenolpyruvate:sugar phosphotransferase system (PTS). The PTS system is found throughout the bacterial kingdom, and is responsible for the coupled phosphorylation and translocation of numerous sugars across the cytoplasmic membrane. PtsI transfers the phosphoryl group from phosphoenolpyruvate (
IPR036618.name: PtsI, HPr-binding domain superfamily

IPR036619.description: The ninR region of Bacteriophage lambda contains two recombination genes, ninB and ninG (rap), that have roles when the RecF and RecBCD recombination pathways of Escherichia coli, respectively, operate on phage lambda. Genetic recombination in phage lambda relies on DNA end processing by Exo to expose 3'-tailed strands for annealing and exchange by beta protein. Phage lambda encodes an additional
IPR036619.name: NinB superfamily

IPR036621.description: tRNA synthetases, or tRNA ligases are involved in protein synthesis. This domain is found in histidyl, glycyl, threonyl and prolyl tRNA synthetases. It is probably the anticodon binding domain.
IPR036621.name: Anticodon-binding domain superfamily

IPR036622.description: LigAB is a protocatechuate 4,5-dioxygenase () that belongs to the extradiol class III enzyme family. The LigA subunit of this enzyme is multi-helical, containing a compact array of six short helices.
IPR036622.name: Dioxygenase LigAB, LigA subunit superfamily

IPR036623.description: Heat shock protein HspQ, also known as YccV, is an Escherichia coli hemimethylated DNA binding protein which has been shown to regulate dnaA gene expression.
IPR036623.name: Hemimethylated DNA-binding domain superfamily

IPR036624.description: This entry consists of Hcp-like proteins. Hcp is part of the type VI secretion system of Gram-negative bacteria. Hcp is not only a secreted effector protein, but also might act as machine component.
IPR036624.name: Hcp1-like superfamily

IPR036625.description: A small domain of the E2 subunit of 2-oxo-acid dehydrogenases that is responsible for the binding of the E3 subunit. Proteins containing this domain include the branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex of bacteria, which catalyses the overall conversion of alpha-keto acids to acyl-CoA and carbon dioxide; and the E3 binding protein of eukaryotic pyruvate dehydrogenase.
IPR036625.name: E3-binding domain superfamily

IPR036626.description: GpW is a 68 residue protein known to be present in phage particles. Extracts of phage-infected cells lacking GpW contain DNA-filled heads, and active tails, but no infectious virions. GpW is required for the addition of GpFII to the head, which is, in turn, required for the attachment of tails. Since GpFII and tails are known to be attached at the connector, GpW is also likely to assemble at this
IPR036626.name: Head-to-tail joining protein W superfamily

IPR036627.description: CobW proteins are generally found proximal to the trimeric cobaltochelatase subunit CobN, which is essential for vitamin B12 (cobalamin) biosynthesis. They contain a P-loop nucleotide-binding loop in the N-terminal domain and a histidine-rich region in the C-terminal portion suggesting a role in metal binding, possibly as an intermediary between the cobalt transport and chelation systems. CobW mig
IPR036627.name: CobW-like, C-terminal domain superfamily

IPR036628.description: ClpA is an ATP-dependent chaperone and part of the ClpAP protease that participates in regulatory protein degradation and the dissolution and degradation of protein aggregates. ClpA recognises sequences in specific proteins, which it then unfolds in an ATP-dependent manner and transports into the degradation chamber of the associated ClpP protein. A small adaptor-like protein, ClpS, modulates the
IPR036628.name: Clp, N-terminal domain superfamily

IPR036629.description: This entry represents a group of bacterial stress response proteins, including CsbD. The expression of CsbD is mediated by sigma-B, an alternative sigma factor. These proteins contain a SAM domain-like fold.

IPR036633.description: Pyridoxal-dependent decarboxylases are bacterial proteins acting on ornithine, lysine, arginine and related substrates. One of the regions of sequence similarity contains a conserved lysine residue, which is the site of attachment of the pyridoxal-phosphate group. Ornithine decarboxylase is a dodecamer composed of six homodimers and catalyzes the decarboxylation of tryptophan. Arginine decarboxyla
IPR036633.name: Orn/Lys/Arg decarboxylase, C-terminal domain superfamily

IPR036635.description: This entry represents a C-terminal conserved region of UDP-N-acetylenolpyruvoylglucosamine reductase, which is also called UDP-N-acetylmuramate dehydrogenase. The C-terminal domain is involved in substrate binding. It is a part of the pathway for the biosynthesis of the UDP-N-acetylmuramoyl-pentapeptide, which is a precursor of bacterial peptidoglycan.
IPR036635.name: UDP-N-acetylenolpyruvoylglucosamine reductase, C-terminal domain superfamily

IPR036636.name: Cytochrome c oxidase subunit VIIc superfamily

IPR036637.description: A number of enzymes that catalyze the transfer of a phosphoryl group from phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) via a phospho-histidine intermediate have been shown to be structurally related. All these enzymes share the same catalytic mechanism: they bind PEP and transfer the phosphoryl group from it to a histidine residue. IPR036637.name: Phosphohistidine domain superfamily

IPR036640.description: This entry represents the transmembrane domain in cases where the TMD and ABC region are found in the same protein, and corresponds to ABC type 1 from Transporter Classification Database.

IPR036641.description: This superfamily represents a domain present at the N terminus in proteins which undergo autophosphorylation. The group includes histidine kinases such as CheA from Escherichia coli, the gliding motility regulatory protein from Myxococcus xanthus, and a number of bacterial chemotaxis proteins.

IPR036643.description: RNA polymerase (RNAP) II, which is responsible for all mRNA synthesis in eukaryotes, consists of 12 subunits. Subunits Rpb3 and Rpb11 form a heterodimer that is functionally analogous to the archaeal RNAP D/L heterodimer, and to the prokaryotic RNAP alpha (RpoA) subunit homodimer. In each case, they play a key role in RNAP assembly by forming a platform on which the catalytic subunits (eukaryotic
IPR036643.name: DNA-directed RNA polymerase, insert domain superfamily

IPR036644.description: Ferredoxin thioredoxin reductase is a [4FE-4S] protein present in organisms performing oxygenic photosynthesis, and plays an important role in the ferredoxin/thioredoxin regulatory chain. It converts an electron signal (photoreduced ferredoxin) to a thiol signal (reduced thioredoxin), regulating enzymes by reduction of specific disulphide groups. IPR036644.name: Ferredoxin thioredoxin reductase catalytic beta subunit superfamily

IPR036646.description: Two distinct classes of phosphoglycerate mutases (PGMs) are known; those dependent on cofactor 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate (2,3-BPG) and those whose activity is independent of cofactor but dependent on the presence of divalent metal cations. IPR036646.name: BPG-independent phosphoglycerate mutase, domain B superfamily

IPR036648.description: Nitrile hydratases () are bacterial enzymes that catalyse the hydration of nitrile compounds to the corresponding amides. They are used as biocatalysts in acrylamide production, one of the few commercial scale bioprocesses, as well as in environmental remediation for the removal of nitriles from waste streams. Nitrile hydratases are composed of two subunits, alpha and beta, and are normally active
IPR036648.name: Nitrile hydratase alpha /Thiocyanate hydrolase gamma superfamily

IPR036649.description: Inorganic pyrophosphatase () (PPase) is the enzyme responsible for the hydrolysis of pyrophosphate (PPi) which is formed principally as the product of the many biosynthetic reactions that utilise ATP. All known PPases require the presence of divalent metal cations, with magnesium conferring the highest activity. Among other residues, a lysine has been postulated to be part of or close to the activ
IPR036649.name: Inorganic pyrophosphatase superfamily

IPR036651.description: Glutamine synthetase () (GS) plays an essential role in the metabolism of nitrogen by catalysing the condensation of glutamate and ammonia to form glutamine. This entry represents the glutamine synthetase N-terminal domain, which adopts a β-grasp fold and contributes to the substrate binding pocket of the enzyme.
IPR036651.name: Glutamine synthetase, N-terminal domain superfamily

IPR036652.description: In bacteria or archaea, YjeF N-terminal domains occur either as single domain proteins or fused with other domains and are commonly associated with enzymes. YjeF N-terminal domains (also known as NAD(P)H-hydrate epimerase) are often fused to a YjeF C-terminal domain. IPR036652.name: YjeF N-terminal domain superfamily

IPR036654.description: DNA-directed DNA polymerase () catalyzes DNA-template-directed extension of the 3'-end of an RNA strand by one nucleotide at a time. DNA polymerase III is a complex, multichain enzyme responsible for most of the replicative synthesis in bacteria. The enzyme also has 3' to 5' exonuclease activity. IPR036654.name: DNA polymerase III, psi subunit superfamily

IPR036660.description: This entry represents various Fe-S type hydro-lyases, including the beta subunit from both L-tartrate dehydratase (TtdB;) and class 2 fumarate hydratase (FumC;). IPR036660.name: Fe-S hydro-lyase, tartrate dehydratase beta-type, catalytic domain superfamily

IPR036661.name: Luciferase-like domain superfamily

The PTS catalyses the phosphorylation of incoming sugar substrates and coupled with translocation across the cell membrane, makes the PTS a link between the uptake and metabolism of sugars.
IPR036662.name: Phosphotransferase system, mannose-type IIA component superfamily

IPR036663.description: Fumarylacetoacetase (; also known as fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase or FAH) catalyses the hydrolytic cleavage of a carbon-carbon bond in fumarylacetoacetate to yield fumarate and acetoacetate as the final step in phenylalanine and tyrosine degradation. IPR036663.name: Fumarylacetoacetase-like, C-terminal domain superfamily

IPR036667.name: Phosphotransferase system, sorbose subfamily IIB component superfamily

IPR036678.description: Mismatch repair contributes to the overall fidelity of DNA replication and is essential for combating the adverse effects of damage to the genome. It involves the correction of mismatched base pairs that have been missed by the proofreading element of the DNA polymerase complex. The post-replicative Mismatch Repair System (MMRS) of Escherichia coli involves MutS (Mutator S), MutL and MutH proteins
IPR036678.name: MutS, connector domain superfamily

IPR036679.description: Flagella synthesis protein FlgN is an export chaperone involved in flagellar synthesis. FlgN consists of a 4 long helices bundle, where the last helix is shorter than the three others. FlgN is required for the export of the hook-filament junction proteins, FlgK and FlgL. It is required for both swimming and swarming motility in B. subtilis.
IPR036679.name: FlgN-like superfamily

SPOR domains can localise to the division site by binding preferent
IPR036680.name: Sporulation-like domain superfamily

It is found in uncharacterised proteins, including YutG from Bacillus subtilis (), putative phosphatidylglycerophosphatases and bacterial phosphatidylglycerophosphatase PgpA.
IPR036681.name: PgpA-like superfamily

IPR036683.description: Proteins containing this domain form structural complexes with other known families, such as and. IPR036683.name: CO dehydrogenase flavoprotein, C-terminal domain superfamily

MoCF is ubiquitous in nature, and the pathway for MoCF biosynthesis is conserved in all three domains of life. MoCF-containing enzymes function as oxidoreductases in carbon, nitrogen, and sulphur metabolism.

IPR036690.description: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases (aaRSs) play a crucial role in the translation of the genetic code by means of covalent attachment of amino acids to their cognate tRNAs. Phenylalanine-tRNA synthetase (PheRS, also known as Phenylalanine-tRNA ligase) is known to be among the most complex enzymes of the aaRS family. IPR036690.name: Ferrodoxin-fold anticodon-binding domain superfamily

These are small, diffusible molecules used as communication signals in a large variety of proteobacteria. It is almost always found in association with the DNA-binding LuxR domain (). IPR036693.name: Transcription factor LuxR-like, autoinducer-binding domain superfamily

IPR036694.description: This entry represents proteins with a Dodecin topology. IPR036694.name: Dodecin-like superfamily

These enzymes vary widely in size and oligomeric state, and share limited sequence homology.

IPR036700.description: Proteins in this entry have an OB-fold fold (oligonucleotide/oligosaccharide binding motif). They contain a predicted N-terminal signal peptide which indicates that they localise to the periplasm where they may function to bind proteins, small molecules, or other typical OB-fol
IPR036700.name: Bacterial OB-fold superfamily

IPR036702.description: 2-phosphosulpholactate phosphatase (ComB;) is a magnesium-dependent acid phosphatase that catalyzes the second step in coenzyme M (CoM; 2-mercaptoethanesulphonic acid) biosynthesis, namely, the hydrolysis of (2R)-2-phospho-3-sulpholactate to yield (2R)-3-sulpholactate and phosphate. These proteins contain a swivelling 3-layer β/β/α domain that appears to be mobile in most multi-domain proteins known to contain it. IPR036704.name: Ribonuclease E inhibitor RraA/RraA-like superfamily

IPR038333.name: Type I restriction enzyme EcoKI-like, methylase subunit, N-terminal domain superfamily

IPR038973.description: Mismatch repair contributes to the overall fidelity of DNA replication by targeting mispaired bases that arise through replication errors during homologous recombination and as a result of DNA damage. IPR038973.name: DNA mismatch repair protein MutL/Mlh/Pms-like

IPR038987.description: Eukaryotic and prokaryotic molybdoenzymes require a molybdopterin cofactor (MoCF or Moco) for their activity. The biosynthesis of this cofactor involves a complex multistep enzymatic pathway. In bacteria, The final step in MoCF synthesis is the attachment of mononuclear Mo to MPT, a process that requires MoeA and which is enhanced by MogA in an Mg2 ATP-dependent manner.

IPR038996.description: This entry includes Gp14 and related proteins from tailed bacteriophages and bacterial prophages. Gp14 is a component of the cylindrical core that assembles on the inner surface of the capsid during capsid formation and plays a role in viral DNA ejection into the host cell.
IPR038996.name: Internal virion protein Gp14

IPR039000.description: DinG is a DNA damage-inducible protein that functions as a helicase which translocates on single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) in the 5'-3' direction. The ATP-dependent DNA helicase activity of DinG requires divalent cations (Mg2+, Ca2+, and Mn2+) but is not observed in the presence of Zn2+.
IPR039000.name: ATP-dependent DNA helicase DinG

IPR039001.description: Peptidoglycan-associated lipoprotein (Pal or OprL) is part of the Tol-Pal system. The system appears to be involved both in the maintenance of outer membrane integrity and in outer membrane invagination during cell division. IPR039001.name: Peptidoglycan-associated lipoprotein

IPR039013.description: YgiF from E. coli is a specific inorganic triphosphatase (PPPase). Inorganic pyrophosphatase (PPase) is the main enzyme responsible for hydrolysis of PPPi, whereas YgiF contributes only marginally to the total PPPase activity in this organism. PPPi could be cytotoxic because of its high affinity for calcium ion, thereby interfering with calcium signaling.
IPR039013.name: Inorganic triphosphatase YgiF

The toxin protein HigB is a ribosome-dependent mRNA interferase belonging to RelE family, which cleave mRNAs at the ribosomal A site. IPR039068.name: Pyrroloquinoline-quinone synthase-like

IPR039121.name: Acyl-coenzyme A diphosphatase NUDT19

IPR039247.name: RNA-binding protein KhpB

IPR039315.name: Chemotaxis protein CheW

IPR039331.name: Purple acid phosphatase-like

YfbR shows strict specificity towards deoxyribonucleoside 5'-monophosphates, and has been established as an essential component of the deoxycytidine pathway for de novo synthesis of thymidylate. IPR039356.name: 5'-deoxynucleotidase YfbR/HDDC2

Och1 is a alpha-1,6-mannosyltransferase involved in the N-linked oligosaccharide modification in the Golgi apparatus with the addition of mannose to the Man 8 GlcNAc 2 or Man 9 GlcNAc 2 endoplasmic reticulum intermediates. IPR039368.name: Acetolactate synthase large subunit, TPP binding domain

IPR039374.name: Siderophore-interacting protein

IPR039375.name: Nodulation protein N-like

While many di-iron enzymes catalyze dioxygen-dependent reactions, manganese catalase performs peroxide-dependent oxidation-reduction. This family includes RNase Rh, RNase MC1, RNase LE, and self-incompatibility RNases (S-RNases). IPR039378.name: Ribonuclease T2, prokaryotic

IPR039393.name: Rhizopine-oxygenase-like

IPR039395.name: Peptidase C39-like A

IPR047596.name: Orotidine 5'-phosphate decarboxylase, bacterial

IPR047610.name: Translesion DNA synthesis-associated protein ImuA

QOR catalyses the conversion of a quinone NAD(P)H to a hydroquinone NAD(P). Quinones are cyclic diones derived from aromatic compounds. IPR047618.name: Quinone oxidoreductase-like

IPR047622.name: GPR1/FUN34/YaaH conserved region

IPR047623.name: Succinate-acetate/proton symporter SatP

IPR047640.description: This entry represents HTH-type transcriptional regulator RpiR-like family of proteins which includes RpiR, MurR, HexR and some uncharacterised transcriptional regulators mainly from bacteria.
IPR047640.name: HTH-type transcriptional regulator RpiR-like

IPR047641.name: ABC transporter, ATP-binding protein MalK/UgpC-like

IPR047651.description: This entry includes the ribosome-associated ATPase RbbA from E. coli and its homologues, found in proteobacteria. IPR047651.name: Ribosome-associated ATPase RbbA

IPR047661.description: This family represents the AAA+ ATPases of IS21 family IS (insertion sequence) elements, known as IstB, which regulates IS21 transposon function. IstB assembles into a clamshell-shaped decamer that sandwiches DNA between two helical pentamers of ATP-associated AAA+ domains. This complex is recognised by IS21 transposase and promotes its disassembly by stimulating ATP hydrolysis.
IPR047661.name: Insertion sequence IS21-like ATPase IstB

IPR047662.description: The SWEET (Sugars Will Eventually be Exported Transporter) is a superfamily of sugar transporters found in both eukaryotes and prokaryotes. Eukaryotic SWEETs usually have seven transmembrane helices (TMHs), but most prokaryotic SWEETs (SemiSWEETs) have only three TMHs. This entry represents prokaryotic SWEETs (SemiSWEETs), which have 3 TMHs.

IPR047676.name: FxLYD domain

IPR047677.description: This entry represents a domain found in a group of uncharacterised prokaryotic selenoproteins. It contains a conserved sequence GDCCVxC. The function of this domain is unknown.

SmrA, also known as YdaL, is a small endonuclease with homology to the C-terminal domain found in the endonuclease MutS2, but not found in the related mismatch repair protein MutS. The biological role of this endonuclease is not yet known.
IPR047688.name: DNA endonuclease SmrA

IPR047691.description: Proteins of this family are components of the exopolysaccharide Pel transporter. This family includes LpxO1 from Pseudomonas aeruginosa (), but not its paralog LpxO2.

IPR047698.name: Nitroreductase subunit ArsF-like

NrtS1 and NrtS2 form a heteromeric transporter complex that was shown to transport nitrite as well as nitrate.

IPR047720.name: Mks condensin complex protein MksB, putative

IPR047767.name: PSP1-like

IPR047770.name: Sensor histidine kinase RegB

IPR047787.name: Phosphoethanolamine transferase EptC/CptA

IPR047794.name: Peptidase C45-like

IPR047801.name: Peptidase C45

IPR047805.name: Cyclic GMP-AMP synthase

IPR064384.description: This entry includes Slr0373. Members of this family, restricted to the Cyanobacteria, average about 115 amino acids in length and contain a central CPxC motif. The N-terminal region resembles DNA-binding ribbon-helix-helix domains such as CopG family transcriptional regulators.
IPR064384.name: Slr0373 blue light stress response protein

IPR064388.description: The founding member of this entry, sll1863 from Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803, was identified first as a salt stress-induced protein and later as a more general stress-induced protein. The sequence has a high concentration of both positively and negatively charged residues, alternating with strongly hydrophobic residues. This domain is found either as standalone or in combination with other domains.
IPR064388.name: Sll1863-like stress response domain

IPR064397.name: Type IV pilus assembly protein PilC, Myxococcales

IPR064398.description: This entry includes type IV pilus assembly protein PilC from Thermus thermophilus and related sequences found in Deinococcales and Thermales. It is a essential inner membrane component of the type IV pilus (T4P) that plays a role in surface and host cell adhesion, colonisation, biofilm maturation, virulence, and twitching, a form of surface-associated motility facilitated by cycles of extension, a
IPR064398.name: Type IV pilus assembly protein PilC, Thermus thermophilus-type

IPR064403.description: This entry represents Transcriptional regulator LdrP which activates transcription. This protein positively regulates PcrtB promoter upstream of the crtB operon in a cAMP-independent manner. It regulated genes include genes encoding DNA photolyase, phytoene synthase and cytochrome P450 monooxygenase, which are involved in carotenoid biosynthesis. LdrP positively regulates the light-inducible gene
IPR064403.name: Transcriptional regulator LdrP

IPR064407.name: Putative type IX sorting system protein PorV2

IPR064418.description: Cdf31, a member of the cation diffusion facilitator (CDF) family of transporters, was shown in Nostoc punctiforme to be induced by zinc, lower intracellular concentrations of zinc, and to be one of several metal efflux transporters contributing to zinc homeostasis.
IPR064418.name: CDF family zinc efflux transporter Cdf31

IPR064420.description: This entry represents a cyanobacterial protein family homologous to the C-terminal galactosyl-1-phosphate transferase domain of the Salmonella bifunctional RfbP, which is involved in O-antigen biosynthesis rather than LPS core biosynthesis. While the homology of this family to undecaprenyl-phosphate galactose phosphotransferases is reflected in the protein name provided here, mirroring current usa
IPR064420.name: Undecaprenyl-phosphate galactose phosphotransferase

IPR064422.name: Response regulator cyclic di-GMP phosphodiesterase PvrR

IPR064426.description: This entry includes 4-hydroxyproline 2-epimerase from Ruegeria pomeroyi and similar proteins from proteobacteria. This protein catalyses the epimerization of trans-4-hydroxy-L-proline (t4LHyp) to cis-4-hydroxy-D-proline (c4DHyp).
IPR064426.name: 4-hydroxyproline epimerase

IPR064434.description: This entry represents the divisome-associated lipoprotein DalA found exclusively in Rhodobacterales. DalA serves as a scaffold to position or modulate the activity of PG transpeptidases that are needed to form envelope invaginations during cell division. Loss of this protein causes defects in cell division and changes the sensitivity to compounds, affecting cell envelope synthesis and function. Da
IPR064434.name: Divisome-associated lipoprotein DalA

IPR064437.description: This entry represents the biofilm-impacting phospholipase BipL from P. aeruginosa and related proteins. Deletion of bipL increased biofilm formation, supporting the idea that BipL is responsible for reducing biofilm formation in strains with unphosphorylated PtsN.
IPR064437.name: Phospholipase BipL

IPR064440.description: This entry represents Lyso-ornithine lipid O-acyltransferase that catalyses the second step in the formation of ornithine lipids, which are phosphorus-free membrane lipids. It can also act as an alternate acyl-sn-glycerol-3-phosphate acyltransferase (AGPAT) to ensure glycerophospholipid production.
IPR064440.name: Lyso-ornithine lipid O-acyltransferase, Rhodobacterales

IPR064452.description: This family represents ribonuclease E from Cyanobacteria. It is an endoribonuclease that plays a central role in rRNA processing and mRNA decay, and probably tRNA processing. It acts on 9S rRNA (the precursor of 5S rRNA) and RNAI, a molecule that controls the replication of ColE1 plasmid. Upon expression in E.coli does not purify with endogenous degradosome proteins. These proteins prefer 5'-monop
IPR064452.name: Ribonuclease E, cyanobacteria

IPR064464.name: Retropepsin-like osmotic stress tolerance peptidase RloA3

IPR064465.description: This entry represents a group of proteins mainly found in gammaproteobacteria, including RloA2 ().
IPR064465.name: Retropepsin-like osmotic stress tolerance peptidase RloA2

IPR064466.description: RloA, a retropepsin-like aspartic protease, occurs in the Rlo (retropepsin-like osmotic stress tolerance peptidase) operon along with RloB (a multiple-spanning membrane protein with a periplasmic inactive transglutaminase domain) and RloC (a RimK-like protein).
IPR064466.name: Retropepsin-like osmotic stress tolerance peptidase RloA

IPR064467.description: This entry represents a group of proteins mainly found in Pseudomonas species, including RimB ().
IPR064467.name: Retropepsin-like aspartic endopeptidase RimB, Pseudomonas

IPR064470.name: PA0061/PA0062-like lipoprotein
